items.title: I Found a Real Estate ‘Unicorn’: 2 Homes, 1 Mortgage, and $187K a Year
items.summary:
Thinking about investing in real estate, but not sure what to buy? Welcome to "My First Deal," where real people spill about how they chose what to invest in, how they found the property, and how that deal is performing. If you have a story to share about your investor journey, email news@realtor.com .

When Steve Kwong ran the numbers on his first traditional investment property, he realized a single broken water heater would wipe out an entire year of profits. 

So, the 48-year-old Orlando Realtor® walked away from the deal. Then, he teamed up with a business partner, Rob Leventhal — owner of STR pricing, a revenue management service —and pivoted to short-term rentals.

They searched for three months before buying what Kwong calls a real estate "unicorn" : two homes on one lot in Pigeon Forge, TN , with one mortgage. Combined, the two homes grossed $187,000 in 2021—a banner year for most short-term rentals.

Here's how they did it.

Inside the budget: 

Max budget: $475,000
Asking price: $479,000
Closing price: $462,000
Down payment: $92,400
Mortgage: $2,390
Taxes: $3,040 

How did your real estate investment journey begin? 

Originally, I was going to buy a long-term rental on a golf course in Apopka, FL , and would be renting to a friend. I got under contract, but decided not to close. I ran the numbers and would have made $300 a month, which is one capital expense away from not making any money in a year. 

How did you decide to invest in a short-term rental (STR)? 

I was talking to my friend Rob, who had friends who wanted to buy STRs. This was 2019. We decided to…
items.t: I Found a Real Estate ‘Unicorn’: 2 Homes, 1 Mortgage, and $187K a Year

items.title: From Honky-Tonks to High-End Estates: Inside Nashville’s Lasting Luxury Boom
items.summary:
Many metros gave up most or even all of their COVID-19 pandemic-era housing market gains, but some kept on trucking, including Nashville, TN .

"Nashville is one of the pandemic boomtowns that kept its boom," writes Realtor.com® senior economist Anthony Smith in his Nashville Luxury Market Highlight report .

Nashville held on to more of its pandemic run-up than any other major Tennessee metro as of September 2026, says the report.

While the area has been hot for years, demand for its luxury homes accelerated sharply after the pandemic, resulting in a 100% increase in prices from February 2020 to October 2026. Unlike other metros that gave up most or even all of its pandemic-era gains, Nashville has retained a healthy 83.3% of them.

During the pandemic, remote work allowed many people to relocate to Music City, where they could enjoy not only the conveniences and excitement of city life, but also lower prices than wherever they were coming from.

Condo units in The Residences start at $1.6 million for a one-bedroom, appealing to the city's surge of corporate high-earners. (DBox) 

And unlike other midsized metros that saw massive pandemic-era gains—such as Denver and Austin, TX—Nashville's prices have kept afloat. Denver, on the other hand, sits 33% below its pandemic peak, and Austin is 29% below.

Nashville's entry-luxury threshold (the top 10% of listings) now stands at $1.65 million versus $899,000 at the start of the pandemic in February 2020. This is only 8.4% below its peak of $1.80 million in April 2022.

In terms of retention, the only Tennessee city that comes…
items.t: From Honky-Tonks to High-End Estates: Inside Nashville’s Lasting Luxury Boom

items.title: Why This Winter Could Be a Hidden Opportunity for Homebuyers—Plus a New Rate Discount From Chase
items.summary:
The housing market remains tough this winter—but prepared buyers will be presented with opportunities.

"Preparation is everything," says Erik Schmitt , head of consumer direct sales at Chase Home Lending, which is part of JPMorgan Chase's commercial bank.

The outlook for 2027 appears tough. The latest Realtor.com® quarterly construction insights report shows that prices on new homes are holding steady, but builders are having to get creative to attract buyers. Many have said they expect difficulty for much of next year.

On top of that, leaders at the Federal Reserve have signaled that they're poised to raise interest rates multiple times in the next few months to tame inflation. Homeowners are also managing rising insurance costs , HOA fees , and utilities .

Do anything you can now to improve your credit, pay down debt, and understand your budget and what you can afford will help, says Schmitt.

"Get pre-approval because you never know when the market will turn," he advises.

Improving credit scores and paying off higher interest-rate debt will give you more purchasing power.

This week, the  National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index  plunged to a 14-year low . Meanwhile, the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Index  showed home values fell for the 16th straight month .

So, in the coming winter there's no question about seasonal weakness in the housing market. In some markets, that means more negotiating power and possibly some better options for buyers. But shrinking inventory might also mean there are fewer options.

items.title: Washington, DC, Struggles with Low Starter Home Availability Compared to Other Cities
items.summary:
For many Americans, the dream of owning a home has felt increasingly out of reach. A recent metro-by-metro analysis of starter home options by Realtor.com® highlights this challenge, as rising prices and climbing mortgage rates compound the difficulties for would-be buyers.

Furthermore, research from economists at Realtor.com shows a national decline in starter home inventory . The share of these homes in active inventory fell from 38.1% in August 2019 to 36.2% in August 2026. During that same period, starter home prices surged by 30.8%, increasing from approximately $260,000 to $340,000. 

In Washington, DC , the findings reveal a downturn in the availability of these crucial entry-level properties in recent years.

Starter home availability sees a slight dip 

A starter home is defined by Realtor.com as a property priced at roughly 80% of a metro's median list price, making it an accessible option for a first-time buyer . These homes are typically smaller and less expensive than the market average, aligning with the affordability needs of households earning at or below the area's median income .

In the DC metro area, the share of starter homes was 33.6% in 2019 and shifted slightly to 33.2% in 2022. As of 2026, the share stands at 33.3%. This represents a -0.3 point change since 2019, highlighting a slight but notable shortfall in entry-level housing options for prospective buyers in the nation's capital.

Renting remains the more affordable option 

For those weighing the decision between renting or buying , current data suggests that renting is the more financially…
items.t: Washington, DC, Struggles with Low Starter Home Availability Compared to Other Cities

items.title: How the Kennedys Spent Thanksgiving at Their Hyannis Port Compound—Where JFK and His Father Plotted a Presidential Run
items.summary:
When John F. Kennedy came home to Hyannis Port for his first Thanksgiving as president, his father still had the best seat in the house. 

Joseph P. Kennedy presided over the family table, the children ate first, and the cranberries served with dinner came from bogs near the family’s Cape Cod retreat. 

Five years earlier, it was what happened after Thanksgiving dinner that the family would remember. John, then a Massachusetts senator, slipped into the study off the living room with his father. 

He had a list of reasons to think twice about running for president. Joseph had an answer for every one.

By the time they emerged, the Kennedys had a campaign to plan . 

When John F. Kennedy came home to Hyannis Port for his first Thanksgiving as president, his father still had the best seat in the house. (Hy Peskin/Getty Images) 

Thanksgiving at the Big House 

The house where that conversation took place began as a summer rental. In 1926, Joseph and his wife, Rose , brought their children to Malcolm Cottage, a waterfront home overlooking Nantucket Sound. John was just 9.

According to the John F. Kennedy Hyannis Museum, Joseph bought the property two years later for $25,000 and expanded the house to accommodate his growing family. 

John eventually bought a place of his own behind his parents’ home. His brother Robert and sister-in-law Ethel came to own an adjoining property. 

Together, the three residences formed the 6-acre compound, an arrangement that put several generations of Kennedys within walking distance of Thanksgiving dinner at the Big House.

items.t: How the Kennedys Spent Thanksgiving at Their Hyannis Port Compound—Where JFK and His Father Plotted a Presidential Run

items.title: Thanksgiving Murder Mystery Remains Unsolved 30 Years After Killer Allegedly Used Cat Door to Enter Woman’s Texas Apartment
items.summary:
For 30 years, Thanksgiving has been a painful reminder for a Texas family whose holiday turned into a nightmare when their loved one was found strangled inside her Houston apartment.

Kristen Lea Wilson , 29, was preparing to spend Thanksgiving with her family in November 1996 when investigators say someone slipped into her first-floor apartment through a window, using a cat door to gain access, and waited for her to return home.

After cutting the telephone cord and unscrewing the lightbulbs to keep the apartment dark, the intruder waited in Wilson’s bedroom closet.

When she never showed up to Thanksgiving dinner the following day, her parents became worried and drove her apartment where they found her slain body. Three decades later, no one has been charged in her murder , and her family is still fighting for answers.

“Thirty years ago this Thanksgiving my sister Kristen Lea Wilson was murdered in Houston,” Kelly Wilson Hancock wrote in a recent social media post. “She was strangled–this was an up and personal murder. Her case has NEVER been solved.”

A killer waiting inside 

On Nov. 27, 1996, the day before Thanksgiving, Wilson stopped at a grocery store after work to pick up last-minute items for the family's holiday gathering at her grandparents' home in Katy, TX.

She returned to her apartment on Meadowglen Lane in southwest Houston, unloaded her groceries, and reportedly went into her bedroom to change clothes. Investigators believe her killer was already inside.

According to the Houston Police Department, the intruder likely gained access by reaching through a…
items.t: Thanksgiving Murder Mystery Remains Unsolved 30 Years After Killer Allegedly Used Cat Door to Enter Woman’s Texas Apartment

items.title: Why the Northeast Could Lead a Factory-Built Housing Boom
items.summary:
Most Americans picture sun-drenched mobile home parks across the South and Southeast when they think of manufactured housing , but more manufactured housing may soon start popping up across the Northeast and West. 

A new economic research report from Realtor.com® senior economist Joel Berner takes an in-depth look at the manufactured housing guidelines in the 21st Century Road to Housing Act, which became law in June. 

Berner found that cities across the Northeast—including Hartford, CT , Allentown, PA , and Albany, NY —have ideal conditions for a manufactured housing boom: “affordable land, unaffordable traditional new construction, and a low share of single-family starter home inventory.”

If you’re not quite sure about what “manufactured housing" means, you’re not alone. For years, people seemingly used “mobile home” and “manufactured housing” interchangeably. But they’re not the same thing.

For one, the “mobile home” classification was retired in 1980, though many still use it colloquially. That year, it was replaced by the term “manufactured home.” Broadly, manufactured homes are those built in a factory and then transported to a site. 

For years, federal Housing and Urban Development code required that all manufactured homes have a permanent steel towing frame underneath. New provisions in the Road to Housing Act, meant to spur more affordable housing, eliminated that requirement.

The act further entitles these new chassis-free homes to the same financing, titling, insurance, taxes, transport, and installation as conventional homes.  

The hope is that creating…
items.t: Why the Northeast Could Lead a Factory-Built Housing Boom

items.title: ‘We Got an Abandoned Mobile Home for Free–and Spent $14K Transforming It’
items.summary:
An Oregon family transformed a mobile home that had sat abandoned for nearly five years into a home for a loved one–all without paying a dime for the property itself .

But getting the home for free was only the beginning. What followed was months of demolition , electrical and plumbing work, drywall installation, and a race to get the aging property ready for its new owner.

Lyman Branson II , who documented the transformation on I Can Fix That , his YouTube channel , took on the ambitious renovation alongside his family with one goal in mind: creating a safe, comfortable home for his sister, Betty Branson , 42, and her 17-year-old twin daughters.

“I don't think I've ever had an opportunity like this before in my life, and so to turn it down would have been a shame,” Betty tells Realtor.com® . “And I know I would have regretted it, so this was probably one of the better decisions I've made in my life.”

The family spent approximately $14,000 transforming the 1977 mobile home—a fraction of what Betty spent on rent in a year. Betty finally moved in the first week of May 2026, and now, just six months later, she is hosting her first Thanksgiving in the home her family helped bring back to life.

How the family acquired an abandoned home for free 

Lyman has worked in rental property maintenance and renovation since 2001, so he knew about the home in his small town of Irrigon, OR , that had been abandoned by the owner about five years earlier.

He discussed taking over the mobile home to renovate it and rent it out to someone in need. The landlord would be able to transfer…

items.title: Judge Upholds Mamdani’s NYC Rent Freeze, Tosses Landlords’ Lawsuit
items.summary:
A Manhattan judge has upheld New York City 's rent freeze for roughly 1 million rent-stabilized apartments , dismissing a lawsuit brought by landlords who argued that the decision was politically predetermined.

In a 20-page ruling issued on Wednesday, New York Supreme Court Justice Brendan T. Lantry found that the city's Rent Guidelines Board had acted within its authority when it voted this summer to freeze rents on both one- and two-year leases.

The landlords, led by Kenilworth Holdings LLC, argued that Mayor Zohran Mamdani had effectively dictated the outcome after campaigning on a promise to freeze rents and appointing board members who supported the policy.

Judge criticizes Mamdani but upholds freeze 

Despite the favorable ruling, Lantry wasn't entirely sympathetic to the mayor. In his final decision, he called Mamdani's campaign promise "reckless and irresponsible." Even so, he concluded that the board had independently considered the evidence before reaching its decision.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani's rent freeze is a central piece of his housing affordability agenda, alongside his Block by Block plan to build 200,000 affordable homes and preserve another 200,000 over the next decade. (NYC Mayor's Office ) 

The freeze passed in June after a landmark 7-1 vote , with only Arpit Gupta , an economist who was appointed to the board in 2022 by Mayor Eric Adams , voting no.

But it was owner-representative Maksim Wynn 's statement that stoked controversy at the meeting, after he raised concerns about the financial health of the city's buildings. Wynn's full statement was…
items.t: Judge Upholds Mamdani’s NYC Rent Freeze, Tosses Landlords’ Lawsuit

items.title: Infamous ‘Hoarders’ Mansion in North Carolina Sells for $3.85 Million After Jaw-Dropping Restoration
items.summary:
A stunning 1929 English Tudor home in Greensboro, NC, that gained notoriety after it appeared in "Hoarders" closed last week for $3.85 million after two years on the market.

The home was built during the Gilded Age for prominent local businessman Julian Price , and designed by New York architect Charles C. Hartmann . 

The 8,616-square-foot home, found at 301 Fisher Park Circle in Greensboro, has over 30 rooms, including eight bedrooms, six full bathrooms, and two half bathrooms.

The Julian Price Home was put on the National Register of Historic Place in 1980, it gained attention in 2017, when it was featured on an episode of A&E’s "Hoarders".

The home was owned, at the time, by interior designer Sandra Cowart . She had lived in the home since 1975, and kept the home in pristine condition for years, even giving tours and renting out rooms, according to a 2017 article from the Chicago Tribune .

After 2005, she became closed off, became a compulsive collector, and her home was ultimately foreclosed on. The home was purchased out of foreclosure by Eric and Michael Fuko-Rizzo for $415,000, a fraction of the property’s value.

The couple transformed the home back to its former glory with their deep knowledge and love of old homes and architecture.

“They were great people to re-do it, Eric and Michael. Michael’s energy and knowledge of loving old places is honestly over the top,” listing agent Kay Chesnutt , of Berkshire Hathaway Home Services , told Realtor.com. “Not many people would even consider redoing something or saving something like that.”

items.title: Mortgage Rates Dip, Offering Moderate Relief to Buyers Ahead of Thanksgiving as Fed Rate Hike Looms
items.summary:
Mortgage rates have pulled back this week as AI investment trade creates volatility in financial markets and Treasury yields fall back below 5%.

The average rate on 30-year fixed home loans dropped to 7.21% for the week ending Nov. 25, down 7 basis points from 7.28% recorded the week before, according to Freddie Mac . For perspective, rates averaged 6.26% one year ago.

“Mortgage rates moved back down this week, offering modest relief for prospective homebuyers heading into the Thanksgiving holiday,” says Sam Khater , Freddie Mac's chief economist.

It is all but guaranteed that the Federal Reserve will raise its benchmark rate to curb inflation at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Dec. 8. 

The looming hike, combined with the persistence of the war in Iran, pushed the 10-year Treasury yield back toward 4.816% this week, putting mortgage rates on an upward trajectory once again. 

The AI investment trade has created volatility in financial markets as investors try to value companies, including the Anthropic IPO, which gave the company a valuation greater than the value of every home currently listed for sale .

AI-generated wealth is already shaping consumer housing behavior , with San Francisco Bay Area buyers and those in other tech hubs leaning toward higher down payments. 

Markets are currently pricing a 97.6% chance of a 25-basis-point increase next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Meanwhile, pending home sales fell to a record low in October , and existing-home sales hit their lowest level since 2010 , as the surge in mortgage rates…
items.t: Mortgage Rates Dip, Offering Moderate Relief to Buyers Ahead of Thanksgiving as Fed Rate Hike Looms

items.summary:
In recent years, social media has been flooded with videos of folks who’ve purchased a tiny home or accessory dwelling unit (ADU) on Amazon .

Touting to have dropped anywhere between $8,000 to $50,000, these homeowners shared the process of just buying a house with the click of a button, along with whatever else ended up in their carts.

But the reality is, Amazon actually prohibits the sale of habitable tiny homes and prefabricated dwellings. Its Seller Central policy explicitly banned complete prefab homes, tiny house kits marketed as living spaces, modular and container homes, and other factory-built housing units.

Despite that, you’re likely to still find listings for tiny homes on the platform, which makes it even more imperative that you learn the ABCs of ADUs.

An ADU defined 

To begin with, ADUs are additional small housing structures built on a property that already has a main home or main structure. Tiny homes are usually freestanding, compact units typically under 400 square feet—sometimes on foundations or other times on wheels like an RV.

But in both cases, the structures are economical and effective ways to achieve additional living space.

"As urban populations swell and sustainability becomes a central focus, the ability to build smaller, energy-efficient homes with reduced environmental impact will be key," says Paul Dashevsky , co-CEO of Maxable , a leader in ADU planning, building, and development.

But while tiny homes and ADUs may indeed be poised to make a positive impact toward solving the housing crisis , potential buyers need to know that you…
items.t: Before Buying a Tiny Home on Amazon, Make Sure You Know the ABCs of ADUs

items.title: The Home Audit That Could Save Homeowners Thousands—and Cost You Only $50
items.summary:
With housing costs skyrocketing, every little bit helps—and sometimes, there are options even longtime homeowners are unaware of. 

For example, a homeowner recently turned to Reddit to vent about humidity and outdoor air entering their home. They received quotes for an energy audit ranging from $100 to $200 and asked if this service is actually worth it. 

Someone from Connecticut replied saying they paid only $50 for the same type of audit, thanks to a subsidy from their electric company—and depending on your location, utility provider, and/or income, you could also qualify for a subsidized or even free energy audit. 

While experts agree that a $50 assessment is less common, even paying a few hundred for one may save you thousands of dollars down the road. That's because it can uncover hidden air leaks that may contribute to higher utility bills and damaging moisture issues.

“When you seal air leaks, you may prevent water vapor inside your house from turning into liquid inside your walls. This eliminates the need for costly wood rot and mold issues that may lead to $5,000 or more in repairs and reduces wear and tear on your HVAC unit,” explains Andrew Pho , a home renovation and improvement expert at Mister Balustealing in Toronto .

What an energy audit entails 

Energy audits are designed to find what’s causing energy loss in your home, but they’re not all created equal. 

Before booking one, confirm what it includes. 

“At the very least, it should consist of a blower-door test (a blower fan is set up in a doorway to measure how much air is leaking in or out of the…
items.t: The Home Audit That Could Save Homeowners Thousands—and Cost You Only $50

"From day one, we all met up, had a little dinner over at their house, and we said, 'We wanna go 1-2,'" she explained to the outlet. "And we didn't specify, like, whatever happens, happens, but the fact that we came in here and we both got those perfect scores. We both did everything we could and it was truly in the hands of the people at home. I'm really proud of what we did and I'm really, really happy that Team USA took it home."

items.title: Thanksgiving Nor’easter Postpones Macy’s Parade and Targets Over 250 Million: The Latest on Power Outages, Homes at Risk, and More
items.summary:
A nor'easter and even a " bomb cyclone " are predicted to slam the Northeast on Thanksgiving this year, putting millions in a path of destruction not seen on the holiday for decades—and causing a time honored tradition to be postponed for the first time in its history. 

Heavy rain, high winds, and coastal impacts to the East Coast are said to begin on Wednesday and carry through Thanksgiving, according to NOAA's Weather Prediction Center .

The biggest impact will be seen starting in the Southeast, before moving its way to the Northeast, Great Lakes, and Ohio Valley.

While flooding is a major consideration, meteorologists are more concerned about the powerful winds accompanying the storm, which could result in tree damage , power outages , and other disasters for homeowners to contend with on the big day. 

The high winds ultimately forced the hands of New York City officials, the NYPD and Macy's, who late on Wednesday announced that the parade would be pushed off until the following Saturday Nov. 28, due to the weather.

The nor’easter 

The storm will ramp up in the Southeast on Wednesday, according to The Weather Channel , with rain, wind, and coastal flooding causing hazardous conditions for travelers heading home for the holiday. 

Because temperatures have dropped as well, snow is also likely in parts of Missouri and Illinois beginning later in the day, continuing into the night, into Thanksgiving.

By Thanksgiving Thursday, the storm will have made its way north into the mid-Atlantic and Ohio Valley, before steadily moving into New England by afternoon or evening.…
items.t: Thanksgiving Nor’easter Could Leave Homeowners In The Dark: Where Power Outages are Likeliest Over The Holiday

items.title: New-Home Sales Surge as Builders Slash Prices to Move Inventory
items.summary:
New -home sales surged in October as prices dropped, according to the latest data from the U.S. Census Bureau.

Sales of new single-family homes hit 701,000 in October, 14.2% above what they were in September and 7.5% above October 2025. Meanwhile, the median sales price hit $391,300, 0.3% below September 2026 and 3.2% below October 2025.

That was driven entirely by a surge in the South, which saw a 36.2% increase from last month and a 24.7% increase from October 2025. Northeast sales plummeted 40.0% month over month and 63.4% year over year, and the Midwest and West also saw declines.

This comes after new-home sales fell 0.6% month over month, 5.3% year over year in September, to 676,000. New-home sales were running 2.9% below 2025 numbers, Realtor.com® economists found. The median sales price in September for new homes fell 3.9% year over year to $400,400.

Realtor.com Senior Economist Joel Berner noted that new home sales are still 3% below where they were in the first 10 months of 2025. And housing inventory remains low.

"Builders are lowering prices to meet demand, and the median new home sales price remains well below the median existing home sales price ," Berner said.

The National Association of Home Builders found that new homes are nearly $40,000 less expensive than existing homes. Single-family housing starts rose 4% last month amid an uneven year . The latest Realtor.com quarterly construction insights report shows that prices on new homes are holding steady, but builders are having to get creative to attract buyers.

Meanwhile, major homebuilders have…
items.t: New-Home Sales Surge as Builders Slash Prices to Move Inventory

items.title: Mortgage Applications Rise to Their Highest Level in 5 Weeks Despite Rise in Rates
items.summary:
Mortgage applications increased last week, despite high interest rates, inflation concerns, and a wobbly stock market. 

For the week ending Nov. 20, the  Mortgage Bankers Association's Market Composite Index —a measure of total mortgage loan application volume—increased 6.1% on a seasonally adjusted basis from one week earlier.

The Purchase Index, which measures the volume of  mortgage applications  to purchase a single-family home, increased 5% from one week earlier after seasonal adjustment, though purchase applications are down 16% from a year ago.

The average contract interest rate for 30-year fixed mortgages with conforming loan balances jumped to 7.38% this week, an increase from last week's rate of 7.31%, according to MBA calculations, and it's the highest level in five weeks.

A separate survey from Freddie Mac showed mortgage rates rose to 7.28%, up from   7.11%  last week. A year ago at this time, the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.26%.

"While mortgage rates increased slightly on a weekly average basis, rates declined over the course of the week, which likely spurred purchase application activity,” said Joel Kan , MBA’s vice president and deputy chief economist.

“Purchase applications reached their strongest weekly pace since September but remained well behind last year’s pace," he added. 

Kan also noted that the share of borrowers relying on riskier adjustable-rate mortgage loans jumped to 11.5%—its highest level in more than a year.

"At 6.39%, the ARM mortgage rate was nearly a full percentage lower than the 30-year fixed rate last week," he…
items.t: Mortgage Applications Rise to Their Highest Level in 5 Weeks Despite Rise in Rates

items.title: Oven Fires Surge This Time of Year—Here Is How Homeowners Can Protect Their Kitchen Over the Holidays
items.summary:
Let’s face it: The holiday season is when our ovens are working overtime. 

After all, between long cooking times for the turkey, the myriad side dishes, and multiple batches of cookies we’re making, this is the season when we put this appliance through the paces. 

Unfortunately, it’s also the prime time for an oven fire.

MoneyGeek recently analyzed seven years of fire department reports to the National Fire Incident Reporting System and compared each state's Thanksgiving Day cooking fires with its own average November day, from 2019 to 2025. Nationally, departments reported 3.72 times as many residential cooking fires on Thanksgiving .

And it's not just the turkey that could get ruined. 

While a professional kitchen remodel averages $26,994, depending on the scope of the project and the location, according to Angi.com , fire damage might amp up that pricetag depending on whether cabinets, drywall, appliances, or partial finishes need to be removed and replaced.

Major structural damage can reach $100,000 if flames or water damaged wiring and plumbing or if the fire spread to adjacent rooms.

This is why experts recommend tried and true precautions homeowners can take to keep their home safe.

From 2019 to 2025, fire departments reported 3.72 times as many residential cooking fires on Thanksgiving as on an average nonholiday November day, according to MoneyGeek. (MoneyGeek) 

Take the time to clean 

In the days leading up to the holidays, be sure to inspect the inside of your oven. 

“Look specifically for older grease buildups,” says Steve Lockwood , owner of…
items.t: Oven Fires Surge This Time of Year—Here Is How Homeowners Can Protect Their Kitchen Over the Holidays

items.title: ‘The Hunting Wives’ Star Malin Akerman Reveals the Private Disco Inside Her New Connecticut Home
items.summary:
Malin Akerman has a private disco in her new Connecticut home, complete with a mixing deck and a smoke machine. 

But ask the star of “The Hunting Wives” where she’s happiest in the house , and she’ll point you to a piece of living room furniture.

“Plopping down on our big pink couch in the living room with my family,” the actress told The Wall Street Jou r nal when he asked about her favorite spot.

Akerman, 48, moved to Connecticut in July with her husband, actor Jack Donnelly , and her son, Sebastian, 13. The family settled into a modern house built in 1988. 

Malin Akerman has a private disco in her new Connecticut home, complete with a mixing deck and a smoke machine. (John Shearer/Getty Images for LACMA) 

“The interior has an inviting flow, and all the rooms are cozy,” she said.

One room in particular gives her a good excuse to send out invitations. Alongside the DJ equipment, Akerman has a disco ball and a laser. “I love to DJ, dance and have friends over for parties,” she said. 

Anyone who ever danced at Akerman’s house in Los Angeles might recognize the decor. In May, when she listed her longtime Hollywood Hills home for $2.9 million, she told Elle Decor that her disco ball would be coming east. 

She had a suggestion for whoever bought the place, too. “I sincerely hope the next owners put in a disco ball,” she said. 

Akerman found that California home while working at a downtown L.A. restaurant. A regular learned she was looking for a rental and offered to show her a house he owned with his brother. 

She spent three years there as a tenant before buying it…
items.t: ‘The Hunting Wives’ Star Malin Akerman Reveals the Private Disco Inside Her New Connecticut Home

items.title: Council tax and stamp duty: both are a disaster zone. Scrap them and start from scratch | Polly Toynbee
items.summary:
These ancient and often grossly unfair taxes are stifling the economy and young people. It’s long past time for radical reform

When voters were asked in 2020 which tax they would cut first, council tax came out on top, and rightly so. Still, it’s taken six years for an array of Labour and Liberal Democrat MPs to call for reforms to this most grotesquely unjust tax.

Prompted by a public petition organised by the campaign Fairer Share, a Westminster Hall debate heard calls for a review into property taxes, which would lay out options for replacing council tax and stamp duty land tax. Labour MPs were among those who have signed a letter to Downing Street calling for property tax reform to be a priority in Andy Burnham’s upcoming 10-year plan. Among flotillas of economists and thinktanks who signed the letter is Lord O’Neill, a Burnham adviser and former Goldman Sachs economist, who calls UK property taxation “utterly nonsensical”. Burnham has frequently backed reform of the “highly regressive” council tax and stamp duty, labelling them as “a tax on the aspiration of young people”.

Polly Toynbee is a Guardian columnist

Continue reading...
items.t: Council tax and stamp duty: both are a disaster zone. Scrap them and start from scratch | Polly Toynbee

Rents on newly agreed lets are forecast to grow by 14.2% between 2026 and 2029, compared with house price growth of 7.2%, according to forecasts from estate agent Hamptons.
